# Fix a backlit portrait (dark face, bright sky)

- Kind: `recipe`
- Category: `photo`
- Slug: `photo/backlit-portrait`

## Summary

Aperture recipe (intermediate). The background must not get brighter with the face.

## Details

### When to use
The subject is dark against a bright background: sun behind the person, a window, a sunset.
### What a pro does and why
The background must not get brighter with the face. A professional compresses the range with the tone layer (pull highlights down hard, open shadows), then lifts only the subject with an exposure layer behind a soft radial mask. Placing the ellipse on the face needs the preview frame; without one, ask where the subject is or suggest the AI subject mask for an exact edge.
### Ops
```json
{
  "summary": "Balance a backlit portrait",
  "ops": [
    {"op": "add_layer", "type": "tone", "params": {"highlights": -55, "shadows": 45, "whites": -10}},
    {"op": "add_layer", "type": "exposure", "params": {"ev": 0.6}, "name": "Subject lift", "mask": {"components": [{"kind": "radial", "center": {"x": 0.5, "y": 0.42}, "rx": 0.28, "ry": 0.38, "feather": 0.6}]}}
  ]
}
```
### How to adjust
Face still dark: raise the masked `ev` to 0.9. A halo appears around the person: increase the radial `feather` to 0.8 or enlarge `rx`/`ry`. Sky looks grey: reduce `highlights` to -35. For a precise outline suggest `subject_mask` (it costs one operation) and reuse its mask.
